solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Coming soon; story about popular German singer

indicators.note: a story going about something wraps itself around it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: something near at hand is nigh
a story is a tale
what is popular is in
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: An entertainment listing announcing a forthcoming feature on a well-loved German vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular German singer' reads as one phrase, but only the last word is the definition; IN and G sit inside the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightingale is a songbird famous for its rich song, so it is literally a singer.

clue.text: Funny maidservant he soon sacked? No way!

indicators.note: a place that has been sacked is plundered and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comic question about whether a household maid will shortly be dismissed, met with a firm refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'sacked' does the shuffling, and every letter of the first four words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an emphatic refusal meaning something will never happen, equivalent to the exclamation.

clue.text: Chivalrous types irritate soldiers

parts.note: to gall is to irritate
soldiers are a caste of ants, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Knights in shining armour get on the nerves of the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallants are courteous, attentive men, especially towards women, which is what chivalry describes.

clue.text: Child touring Antipodes on vacation gets brown

indicators.note: touring a place means travelling all round it, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied of its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A youngster on holiday in Australia comes home with a suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast bread is to brown it under heat, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Draw spirit sent back to see Scrooge

indicators.note: what is sent back travels the opposite way, so in a down clue the pair is read upwards

parts.note: to drag is to draw or pull
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Pull out a bottle of spirits and send it back in disgust at a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a stingy person, and Scrooge from Dickens is the byword for a miser.

clue.text: Vitriolic writer supporting expert on right

indicators.note: in a down answer, something supporting sits underneath, so the writer comes last

parts.note: an ace is an expert
R is the abbreviation for right; on means attached to the expert
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, so a writer

explanation.surface: A savage pundit backs an authority on right-wing politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but here it is a pen, the Bic ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic and vitriolic both describe bitterly sharp, caustic words or manner.

clue.text: Retired film star embracing extremely tender fan

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a former actor is an ex-actor
the extreme letters of the word

explanation.surface: A movie star who has stepped back hugs a devoted admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' pretends to be an admirer, but it is the machine: an extractor fan in a kitchen or bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor is a ventilation device, usually a motorised fan that draws out stale air or steam.

clue.text: Poles defending international wrongdoing

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so the outer pieces enclose the middle one

parts.note: the two poles are South and North
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Polish people shield a global misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality, but it means the North and South Poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a moral offence, a piece of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Unkempt seabird finally finding sanctuary

parts.note: the shag is a seabird of the cormorant family

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the two words after it

parts.note: last letter of the word
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dishevelled seabird at last reaches a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaggy describes hair or fur that is long and untidy, synonymous with unkempt.

clue.text: Necessity will reportedly provoke reaction

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: necessity is need, and will contracts to 'll

explanation.surface: A sentence of social theory: being in want stirs a response.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to goad or irritate them deliberately, trying to get a rise out of them.

clue.text: Construction making a comeback in central Liverpool

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the way you came, so the letters read from right to left
in says the letters are sitting inside the following words, running across the word break

parts.note: the letters straddling the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A football club staging a revival in the heart of Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is a football club, which the comeback suggests, but here 'Construction' is a building; the letters straddle the end of 'central' and the start of 'Liverpool'.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large house, a building, so a construction in the sense of something built.

clue.text: Go out with morsel for Spooner's dog

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: a grain is a tiny morsel; it takes the opening sound of the other word
to go out with someone is to date them; it takes the opening sound of the other word

explanation.surface: An invitation to dinner with a tasty titbit for a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant breed of dog, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Morning in Borstal ruined Sunday lunch?

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: AM marks the morning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreary weekend meal at a young offenders' institution.
explanation.walkthrough: A borstal was a British reform school for young offenders; the question mark marks the definition as one example of a Sunday lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast lamb is a classic British Sunday dinner, so it is an example signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Supernatural apparition laid bare risk and left

indicators.note: laying something bare strips off its covering, so the outside letters are removed

parts.note: a risk is a danger
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A ghostly figure exposes the peril and departs.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a heavenly spirit, and appearances of angels are a kind of otherworldly vision.

clue.text: Editing software originally designed by retired school secretary

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn, gone back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

indicators.note: originally points to the very first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A program built by a former school administrator who has now stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known public school; 'by' means next to, putting the initial after the school secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Notepad is the basic text editor bundled with Microsoft Windows, a piece of software for editing files.

clue.text: Depiction of gateway blocked by beam

indicators.note: a passage blocked by something has that thing lodged in its middle

parts.note: a portal is a gateway
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A painting of an entrance obstructed by a timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' suggests a wooden joist, but it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a representation of someone or something, the same as a depiction.

clue.text: Shrewd copper evacuated theatre

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: an evacuated building has had its contents cleared out, leaving just the shell of first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A clever policeman clears the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is a policeman in the surface but the metal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in its older, chiefly American sense means clever or sharp-witted, as in a cute move.

clue.text: Another broadcast about independent, unconventional protagonist

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the single letter
seed broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A second TV airing of a show about a free-thinking lead character.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character lacking conventional heroic qualities, a protagonist who breaks the usual mould.

clue.text: State again starts to rouse extreme resistance, stopping benefit

indicators.note: something stopping a hole is plugged inside it, so one piece sits within the other
the starts of the next words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letter of the word
first letter of the word
an asset is a benefit or advantage
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A protest slogan: wake up fierce opposition and block the welfare payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extreme' looks like it describes the resistance, but it is just one of the words whose start is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassert something is to declare it once more, which is what stating again means.

clue.text: Shot dead 28's mate

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead
28 across is the female sheep, whose mate is the male

explanation.surface: A grim report of a gunshot killing a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' pretends to be gunfire, but it is a measure of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small drink of spirits, a shot of whisky in Scottish usage.

clue.text: See 1
Israeli's neighbour denied a say about medical instrument

indicators.note: being denied a thing means going without it, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: Syria borders Israel

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, so say

explanation.surface: A diplomatic snub: a neighbouring state refused a voice in talks over medical equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A syringe is the plunger-and-needle device used to inject or withdraw fluids, a standard medical tool.

clue.text: See 1
Suppress content of podcast if left-wing

indicators.note: the content of something is what lies inside it, so the letters are found within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Censoring a podcast's material when it leans to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle something is to hold it back or smother it, synonymous with suppress.

clue.text: Celebrity against taking drug to stop consumption?

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so the drug letter goes inside the pair

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
v, versus, means against
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A famous campaigner against drug-taking, hoping to end its use.
explanation.walkthrough: STAR then V with E inside, which here simply lands after it; 'consumption' reads as drug use but means eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, so eating, or consumption, stops; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Coach trip essentially heading west across Thailand

indicators.note: the essence is the middle, and heading west in an across answer means running right to left, so the core alone is turned round
lying across something means stretching over it, so the trip letters straddle the single letter

parts.note: a tour is a trip
T is the international vehicle registration code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A bus journey travelling westwards through Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus that suits the trip, but it is the teacher. Only the middle pair of the trip is turned round before the Thailand letter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher, and to coach someone is to tutor them, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Nurse worked with nine religious communities

indicators.note: material that has been worked is kneaded into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse put in shifts alongside nine monastic orders.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, nursing was traditionally the work of nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Nunneries are convents, houses where communities of nuns live under religious vows.

clue.text: Scoff at entering trading alliance with Portugal

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the short word sits within the alliance

parts.note: the EU, European Union, is a trading bloc
taken as written
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal, added on

explanation.surface: Mocking the idea of joining a trade bloc alongside Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff at' looks like a phrase meaning mock, but the definition is 'Scoff' alone, in its sense of eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it hungrily, and to eat up is to finish it off greedily.

clue.text: Plant manager's heart set on exchanging frosty greeting

indicators.note: in an across answer, something set on another is placed after it
exchanging places means swapping positions, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
hi is a greeting

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: middle letter of manager

explanation.surface: A factory boss and staff exchange chilly hellos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory to go with the manager, but it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a flowering shrub with bright yellow spring blossom, an example of a garden plant.

clue.text: Topic of article written by setter…

parts.note: the is the definite article
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The subject of a piece composed by the puzzle's author, running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 28 across; in crosswords the setter means me.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a piece of writing or discussion.

clue.text: …solver read out for docile female

indicators.note: something read out is spoken, so the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: the setter addresses the solver as you

explanation.surface: Continuing 27, the solver reads the piece aloud to a meek woman.
explanation.walkthrough: As the setter is me, the solver is you.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, and sheep are proverbially meek and compliant animals.

clue.text: Claim foes regularly drink alcohol? It keeps you animated!

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A drinker insists their enemies' booze is what keeps them lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animated' suggests lively, but here it means kept alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Life-support equipment sustains vital functions in a patient, literally keeping them alive, which is the root sense of animated.
